newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM non-mining subsidiary to be liquidated.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM non-mining subsidiary to be liquidated.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) announced on Friday it had begun liquidating its non-mining subsidiary Mulungushi Investments as part of a continuing programme to rationalise its operations.

"The process of winding up Mulungushi Investments has started in collaboration with the Zambia Privatisation Agency. This will take the normal course of completion," Sam Ekwamo, company manager for corporate affairs, told Reuters in an interview.
He said all companies under Mulungushi Investments had either been privatised or attached to ZCCM in the interim.

Companies under Mulugushi Investments included Mulungushi Traveller, a public transport firm, Nchanga Farms, Sawmilling and Joinery, Rycus Heavy Haulage, Circuit Safaris, Construction Division and Mpelembe Properties.
The disposal of ZCCM's non-mining companies is part of a rationalisation started in December 1993 following a drop in earnings caused by maintenance problems and poor copper prices.
The company suspended capital expenditure projects, closed loss-making operations and withdrew employee benefits as part of the survival plan.
By the end of the 1994/95 financial year, it had cut its labour force to around 45,000 from 56,000 in 1991/92.
The mining conglomerate is being offered for sale as part of an economic reform programme under which the government intends to withdraw from key economic activities.
